note: Potentiators (ivacaftor) and correctors (lumacaftor, tezacaftor, elexacaftor, vanzacaftor) prescribed by CFTR genotype; the pivotal preclinical model is Ussing-chamber chloride transport in primary bronchial epithelia (HBE) cultured from CF patients.
label: Cystic fibrosis (CFTR modulators)

engagement.note: Ivacaftor raised chloride secretion ~10-fold, to ~50% of non-CF, in primary bronchial epithelia from G551D/F508del patients; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: Ivacaftor rescues chloride in patient HBE cells
engagement.quote: VX-770 also increased Cl− secretion in cultured human CF bronchial epithelia (HBE) carrying the G551D gating mutation on one allele and the F508del processing mutation on the other allele by approximately 10-fold
engagement.judgement: Quote is the first 32 words of a 45-word abstract sentence (truncated to the limit). Abstract-level reading.

engagement.note: Phase 2: ivacaftor 150 mg cut sweat chloride 59.5 mmol/L and shifted nasal potential difference, the in-vivo read-outs of the CFTR current HBE cells predicted.
engagement.quote: the median change in the level of sweat chloride was −59.5 mmol per liter (range, −66.0 to −19.0; P=0.008 within-subject, P=0.02 vs. placebo)
engagement.reason: Sweat chloride fell as HBE predicted
engagement.judgement: Earliest in-source comparison: the paper's own background states VX-770 'has been shown to increase the activity of wild-type and defective cell-surface CFTR in vitro' and then reports sweat chloride and NPD in patients. Quote is a verbatim clause of a longer results sentence. Corrector papers (Keating 2018, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1807120; Davies 2018, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1807119) repeat the HBE-plus-sweat-chloride pattern in one paper without changing the status. The F508del-homozygous sweat-chloride non-response (Flume 2012) was not verified within budget, so no 'neg' here.

dose.note: HBE assays give an EC50, but ivacaftor's 150 mg dose was set from clinical exposure–response (FDA review), not from the cell EC50.
dose.short: Cell EC50 not used to set dose
dose.quote: Here we describe the in vitro pharmacology of VX-770, an orally bioavailable CFTR potentiator in clinical development for the treatment of CF.
dose.judgement: FDA clinical pharmacology review, NDA 203188 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203188Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf): 'The proposed dose and dosing regimen is based on exposure-response analysis of dose finding study (vx06-770-101).' Clinical EC50s were 28 ng/mL (FEV1) and 48 ng/mL (sweat chloride); the review contains no comparison of the HBE EC50 with patient exposure.

dose.note: Sweat chloride in healthy people, carriers and patients on modulators at different doses tracked CFTR chloride current in matching HBE cells.
dose.short: HBE current tracks sweat chloride by dose
dose.quote: Sweat chloride concentrations in vivo correlated strongly with CFTR-dependent chloride current in HBE cells in vitro.
dose.reason: HBE chloride current tracks sweat chloride
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the paper compares modulator-treated patients 'at different doses' with chloride transport in corresponding HBE cells, so it is a published dose-level model-vs-patient comparison; but it is a pharmacodynamic-scale calibration, not an EC50-vs-exposure check. Abstract-level reading only (J Cyst Fibros). A stricter reading keeps dose at untested.

efficacy.note: Chloride rescue in patient HBE cells was taken as the proxy for clinical benefit; no patient outcome yet.
efficacy.short: HBE chloride rescue as benefit proxy
efficacy.quote: These results support the hypothesis that pharmacological agents that restore or increase CFTR function can rescue epithelial cell function in human CF airway.

efficacy.note: STRIVE: ivacaftor improved FEV1 by 10.6 points vs placebo in G551D patients, the genotype HBE cells had rescued.
efficacy.quote: The change from baseline through week 24 in the percent of predicted FEV1 was greater by 10.6 percentage points in the ivacaftor group than in the placebo group (P<0.001).
efficacy.judgement: The abstract does not itself cite the HBE model; juxtaposed with Van Goor 2009 (comparison_stated false). Accurso 2010 reported FEV1 within-subject only (P=0.56 vs placebo) so was not used for efficacy. The FDA 2012 review (next entry) states the in-vitro-to-clinical link in one document.

efficacy.note: FDA review: HBE cells showed only limited ivacaftor response in F508del/F508del; the F508del-homozygous trial (Study 104) found no FEV1 effect.
efficacy.quote: Ivacaftor was not effective in subjects who were homozygous for the F508del mutation, with adjusted mean absolute change in FEV1 from baseline through week 16 of 1.5% in ivacaftor group and -0.2% in placebo group
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: scored 'neg' because the same review reports the model flag ('Increased chloride transport in response to ivacaftor were limited in a number of other CFTR genotypes, including G542X/F508del (defective synthesis), F508del/F508del (trafficking)...') and the failed F508del-homozygous trial (treatment difference 1.72%, 95% CI -0.6 to 4.1). It is a genotype-level failure of an approved drug, not a whole-program failure; a stricter reading keeps 'same'. Quote is a verbatim 35-word clause of a 48-word sentence. Review sections 2.6.3 and 3.1.1 (pages 24 and 78).

safety.note: Juvenile rats dosed postnatal day 7–35 developed cataracts at ≥10 mg/kg/day (0.12× MRHD); added to the label August 2012, no patient cases yet.
safety.quote: Cataracts were seen in juvenile rats dosed with ivacaftor from postnatal day 7-35 at dose levels of 10 mg/kg/day and higher (approximately 0.12 times the MRHD based on summed AUCs of ivacaftor and its metabolites).
safety.judgement: The January 2012 original label (203188lbl.pdf) carries no cataract or juvenile-rat text (checked); the finding first appears in section 13.2 of the August 2012 revision (s001), with no warning in section 5 yet.

safety.note: Label §5.3 pairs the rat cataracts with non-congenital lens opacities reported in children ≤12 on ivacaftor; risk 'cannot be excluded'.
safety.short: Pediatric lens opacities followed rat cataracts
safety.quote: Cases of non-congenital lens opacities/cataracts have also been reported in pediatric patients up to 12 years of age treated with KALYDECO.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: causality in patients is not established (confounders: corticosteroids, radiation; the label says only that a risk 'cannot be excluded'); scored 'same' because the label's own §5.3 puts the rat finding and the patient reports side by side. The exact 2014 revision that introduced §5.3 (s004, s008, s007 or s014) was not pinned; the year is unaffected because 2013 carried only CMC supplements and the August 2012 label had no warning. Trikafta's later drug-induced liver injury/liver failure warning (DailyMed setid f354423a-85c2-41c3-a9db-0f3aee135d8d, revised 3/2026) was not predicted by animal toxicology, but no source makes that comparison, so no 'contra'.
